perspective:
Ethan Mohamud’s available information:

- He knows Gary Guo is his close, long-time friend from middle school and works as a doctor/hospital professional.
- He has observed Gary working excessively long hours, skipping meals, and sacrificing sleep, and he became concerned about Gary’s health.
- He invited Gary to a weekend retreat, telling him his health matters and that he hates seeing him like this. He heard Gary decline, saying he appreciated the concern but could not go because there was too much to do at the hospital.
- At the retreat, he observed Gary acting restless and avoiding discussions about work. He suspected there was more than professional obligation behind Gary’s overworking.
- He told Gary they had been friends since middle school and that Gary could tell him anything, without judgment. He heard Gary say it was complicated and that he didn’t want to burden him.
- Gary then opened up to Ethan about pressures from managing a new department and personal challenges. Ethan offered to help prioritize tasks and delegate responsibilities. He heard Gary agree and say he needed help organizing his schedule to make time for himself.
- Over the following months, Ethan regularly checked in with Gary. He heard Gary report improvement, say he was less overwhelmed, and mention having time for a movie the previous weekend. Ethan felt proud and hopeful and offered continued support.
- After about a year, Ethan saw Gary managing a healthier work-life balance on his own. He felt satisfied and happy for Gary, decided to step back, and told Gary he was always a call away if needed and that he knew Gary could handle it. He heard Gary thank him, say he couldn’t have done it without Ethan’s support, and that he felt more in control.
